references.text: Moses exhorts Israel to circumcise the foreskin of their hearts, which connects to the concept of an 'uncircumcised heart' in Leviticus 26:41
The Lord promises to circumcise the people's hearts, pointing back to the uncircumcised heart that must be humbled
Jeremiah speaks of circumcising the heart, the same theme as the uncircumcision of the heart in Leviticus
Jeremiah refers to those who are uncircumcised in heart, a direct parallel to the expression in Leviticus 26:41
Ezekiel speaks of those uncircumcised in heart who profaned the temple
The continuation of the same passage where they must make amends for their own sake, paralleling making atonement for their wrongdoing
God promises to hear when the people humble themselves, which corresponds to the humbling of the uncircumcised heart
Rehoboam and the leaders humbled themselves, and the Lord turned away his wrath—an example of a humbled heart
Stephen calls his opponents 'uncircumcised in heart and ears,' with a direct reference to this Old Testament concept
Paul explains that true circumcision is the circumcision of the heart by the Spirit, not by the letter
